problem: Language-driven InstanceObjectNav assumes a detailed target description is given before navigation, which is impractical for users, and existing ObjectNav/InstanceNav methods fail when many same-category distractors exist. Prior interactive work uses templated Q&A or pre-built maps.
motivation: Users often can only say 'Find the picture'; the agent must resolve visual ambiguity during navigation via natural dialogue while minimizing user effort. This requires deciding when to ask and what to ask, and VLM hallucinations make the agent's perception of candidates unreliable.
key_idea: A training-free plug-in on top of VLFM: a Self-Questioner (LLM-VLM self-dialogue with normalized-entropy uncertainty filtering) produces a reliable description of each detection, and an Interaction Trigger uses an LLM alignment score against known target facts to stop, skip, or ask the user.
insight: Both components are needed: on the ablation split, no components gives SR 9.21 / NQ 3.57, Self-Questioner only 9.87 / NQ 4.6, Skip-Question only 8.55 / NQ 2.69, both 14.47 / NQ 1.68, so reliable perception makes the questions worthwhile and score-based skipping makes them cheap. Normalized entropy over a 3-way Yes/No/IDK vocabulary is a more reliable and threshold-robust uncertainty measure than energy score, LP or MaxProb (Phi 21.12 vs 20.45/14.01/15.94). VLFM alone reaches ~0% SR because it stops at distractors (Distractor Success 3.37/0.84/4.58), showing the bottleneck is instance discrimination.
method: Base policy: VLFM zero-shot frontier exploration (occupancy map + BLIP-2 value map), with Grounding-DINO detection, actions Forward 0.25m/Turn 15°/Stop plus new Ask.
Detection description enrichment: on detection, the VLM produces S_init; the LLM (GPT-4o) generates detail questions given S_init and facts F; VLM answers are concatenated into S_enriched.

Perception uncertainty estimation: VLM is forced to answer Yes/No/I don't know (w=3); normalized Shannon entropy u=H/log(w); certain if u<=tau=0.75. A detection-check prompt must return Yes with Certain, otherwise exploration continues.
Description refinement: LLM extracts attribute-value pairs, generates attribute self-questions, VLM answers with uncertainty, and the LLM filters uncertain attributes to give S_refined.

Interaction Trigger: LLM scores alignment s of S_refined against facts F (and drafts a question in the same call); s>=7 stops, s<5 skips and continues exploring, otherwise asks the user (max 4 rounds) and appends the answer to F.

CoIN-Bench and simulated user: 1,649 GOAT-Bench-derived multi-instance episodes (~5 distractors); user answers simulated by a VLM with a 1024x1024 target image, validated against 40 real-human episodes.
IDKVQA: 502 questions over 102 images with 3 annotators each, used to evaluate uncertainty estimators via Effective Reliability.

setting.backbone: VLFM (BLIP-2, Grounding-DINO, PointNav policy) + LLaVA-1.6 Mistral-7B (VLM) + GPT-4o (LLM), all frozen
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with odometry; category name only as goal
setting.action_space: low-level Forward 0.25m, Turn Left/Right 15°, Stop, Ask (open-ended question)
setting.privileged: simulated user has a high-resolution target image and answers truthfully; agent itself has none

results: On CoIN-Bench AIUTA reaches SR 7.42/14.38/6.67 (Val Seen/Synonyms/Unseen) with under 2 questions on average, versus the zero-shot VLFM's ~0% SR (about 7-14x improvement). It beats trained baselines on Val Unseen (PSL 4.58, OVON 2.61, Monolithic 0.22) but is below OVON on Val Seen Synonyms (15.88) and, in SR, on Val Seen (PSL 8.78, OVON 8.18). Human and simulated users give the same SR (42.50).
limitations: Relies on large LLMs (GPT-4o), with high latency (~11s+8s+6s per invocation) that hinders on-board real-time use.
Absolute success rates remain low (<15%), and the user is assumed to be truthful and fully knowledgeable; the simulated user is a VLM with a target image.
Interaction is limited to attribute questions, not action instructions; evaluated only in simulation.
